# 1 Kings Chapter 22 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** And-they-sat three years — there-was-no war between Aram and-Israel.

**2** And-it-was in-the-third year, and-Jehoshaphat king-of Judah went-down to the-king-of Israel.

**3** And-the-king-of Israel said to-his-servants, "Do-you-know that Ramoth-gilead is ours, and-we are-silent from-taking-it from-the-hand-of the-king-of Aram?"

**4** And-he-said to-Jehoshaphat, "Will-you-go with-me to-battle at-Ramoth-gilead?" And-Jehoshaphat said to the-king-of Israel, "As-I-am, so-are-you; as-my-people, so-are-your-people; as-my-horses, so-are-your-horses."

**5** And-Jehoshaphat said to the-king-of Israel, "Inquire, please, today for-the-word-of YHWH."

**6** And-the-king-of Israel gathered ʾet-the-prophets — about four-hundred men — and-said to-them, "Shall-I-go against Ramoth-gilead to-battle, or-shall-I-refrain?" And-they-said, "Go-up, and-the-Lord will-give-it into-the-hand-of the-king."

**7** And-Jehoshaphat said, "Is-there-not here yet a-prophet-of YHWH, and-we-may-inquire through-him?"

**8** And-the-king-of Israel said to-Jehoshaphat, "There-is yet one man to-inquire-of YHWH through-him, but-I hate-him, for he-does-not prophesy good concerning-me, but evil — Micaiah son-of Imlah." And-Jehoshaphat said, "Let-not the-king say so."

**9** And-the-king-of Israel called a-certain officer and-said, "Hurry — Micaiah son-of Imlah."

**10** And-the-king-of Israel and-Jehoshaphat king-of Judah were-sitting, each on his-throne, clothed in-robes, on-a-threshing-floor at-the-entrance-of the-gate-of Samaria. And-all the-prophets were-prophesying before-them.

**11** And-Zedekiah son-of Chenaanah made for-himself horns-of iron and-said, "Thus says YHWH: 'With-these you-will-gore Aram until-you-finish-them.'"

**12** And-all the-prophets were-prophesying so, saying, "Go-up to-Ramoth-gilead and-prosper, and-YHWH will-give-it into-the-hand-of the-king."

**13** And-the-messenger who went to-call Micaiah spoke to-him, saying, "Behold, please, the-words-of the-prophets are-with-one mouth good to the-king. Let-your-word be, please, like-the-word-of one-of-them, and-speak good."

**14** And-Micaiah said, "As-YHWH lives, what YHWH says to-me — that I-will-speak."

**15** And-he-came to the-king, and-the-king said to-him, "Micaiah, shall-we-go to-Ramoth-gilead to-battle, or-shall-we-refrain?" And-he-said to-him, "Go-up and-prosper, and-YHWH will-give-it into-the-hand-of the-king."

**16** And-the-king said to-him, "How-many times must-I-make-you-swear that you-speak to-me nothing but truth in-the-name-of YHWH?"

**17** And-he-said, "I-saw all Israel scattered upon the-mountains, like sheep that have no shepherd. And-YHWH said, 'These have-no master. Let-them-return, each-man to-his-house, in-peace.'"

**18** And-the-king-of Israel said to-Jehoshaphat, "Did-I-not say to-you, he-does-not prophesy good concerning-me, but evil?"

**19** And-he-said, "Therefore hear the-word-of YHWH: I-saw YHWH sitting on his-throne, and-all the-host-of heaven standing beside-him, on-his-right and-on-his-left.

**20** And-YHWH said, 'Who will-entice Ahab, and-he-will-go-up and-fall at-Ramoth-gilead?' And-one said thus, and-another said thus.

**21** And-the-spirit came-out and-stood before YHWH and-said, 'I will-entice-him.'

**22** And-YHWH said to-him, 'How?' And-he-said, 'I-will-go-out and-be a-lying spirit in-the-mouth-of all his-prophets.' And-he-said, 'You-will-entice, and-you-will-also prevail. Go-out and-do so.'

**23** And-now, behold — YHWH has-put a-lying spirit in-the-mouth-of all these your-prophets, and-YHWH has-spoken evil concerning-you."

**24** And-Zedekiah son-of Chenaanah drew-near and-struck Micaiah on-the-cheek and-said, "Which way did the-Spirit-of YHWH pass from-me to-speak to-you?"

**25** And-Micaiah said, "Behold, you will-see on-that day when you-go into an-inner chamber to-hide."

**26** And-the-king-of Israel said, "Take Micaiah and-return-him to-Amon the-governor-of the-city and-to-Joash the-son-of the-king.

**27** And-say, 'Thus says the-king: Put this-one in-the-house-of confinement, and-feed-him bread-of affliction and-water-of affliction, until I-come in-peace.'"

**28** And-Micaiah said, "If you-surely-return in-peace, YHWH has-not spoken by-me." And-he-said, "Hear, peoples — all-of-you!"

**29** And-the-king-of Israel and-Jehoshaphat king-of Judah went-up to-Ramoth-gilead.

**30** And-the-king-of Israel said to-Jehoshaphat, "I-will-disguise-myself and-go into-the-battle, but-you — put-on your-robes." And-the-king-of Israel disguised-himself and-went into-the-battle.

**31** And-the-king-of Aram had-commanded ʾet-the-commanders-of the-chariots that were-his — thirty-two — saying, "Do-not fight with-small or-great, except with-the-king-of Israel alone."

**32** And-it-was when-the-commanders-of the-chariots saw Jehoshaphat, and-they said, "Surely it is the-king-of Israel." And-they-turned-aside against-him to-fight. And-Jehoshaphat cried-out.

**33** And-it-was when-the-commanders-of the-chariots saw that he was-not the-king-of Israel, and-they-turned-back from-after-him.

**34** And-a-man drew the-bow in-his-innocence and-struck ʾet-the-king-of Israel between the-joints and-the-armor. And-he-said to-his-charioteer, "Turn your-hand and-take-me-out from-the-camp, for I-am-wounded."

**35** And-the-battle went-up on-that day, and-the-king was-propped-up in-the-chariot facing Aram, and-he-died in-the-evening. And-the-blood-of the-wound poured-out into-the-bottom-of the-chariot.

**36** And-the-cry passed-through the-camp as-the-sun went-down, saying, "Each-man to-his-city, and-each-man to-his-land!"

**37** And-the-king died and-was-brought to-Samaria. And-they-buried the-king in-Samaria.

**38** And-they-washed ʾet-the-chariot by the-pool-of Samaria, and-the-dogs licked ʾet-his-blood — and-the-prostitutes bathed — according-to-the-word-of YHWH that he-spoke.

**39** And-the-rest-of the-acts-of Ahab and-all that he-did, and-the-ivory house that he-built, and-all the-cities that he-built — are-they not written in-the-Book-of the-Chronicles-of the-Kings-of Israel?

**40** And-Ahab lay-down with his-fathers. And-Ahaziah his-son reigned in-his-place.

**41** And-Jehoshaphat son-of Asa became-king over Judah in-the-fourth year-of Ahab king-of Israel.

**42** Jehoshaphat was thirty-five years old when-he-became-king, and-twenty-five years he-reigned in-Jerusalem. And-the-name-of his-mother was Azubah daughter-of Shilhi.

**43** And-he-walked in-all the-way-of Asa his-father. He-did-not turn-aside from-it, doing the-right in-the-eyes-of YHWH. Only the-high-places were-not removed; the-people were-still sacrificing and-burning-incense on-the-high-places.

**44** And-Jehoshaphat made-peace with the-king-of Israel.

**45** And-the-rest-of the-acts-of Jehoshaphat and-his-might that he-did and-how he-fought — are-they not written in-the-Book-of the-Chronicles-of the-Kings-of Judah?

**46** And-the-rest-of the-cult-prostitutes that remained in-the-days-of Asa his-father, he-removed from the-land.

**47** And-there-was-no king in-Edom; a-deputy was king.

**48** Jehoshaphat made ships-of Tarshish to-go to-Ophir for-gold, but-they-did-not go, for the-ships were-broken at-Ezion-geber.

**49** Then Ahaziah son-of Ahab said to-Jehoshaphat, "Let-my-servants go with your-servants in-the-ships." But-Jehoshaphat would-not.

**50** And-Jehoshaphat lay-down with his-fathers and-was-buried with his-fathers in-the-City-of David his-father. And-Jehoram his-son reigned in-his-place.

**51** Ahaziah son-of Ahab became-king over Israel in-Samaria in-the-seventeenth year-of Jehoshaphat king-of Judah, and-he-reigned over Israel two years.

**52** And-he-did the-evil in-the-eyes-of YHWH and-walked in-the-way-of his-father and-in-the-way-of his-mother and-in-the-way-of Jeroboam son-of Nebat, who caused Israel to-sin.

**53** And-he-served the-Baal and-bowed-down to-him and-provoked YHWH, the-God-of Israel, according-to-all that his-father had-done.

**54** [End of 1 Kings]

---
## EMET Textual Notes

1. **22:14 — "what YHWH says to-me — that I-will-speak"**: Micaiah's prophetic oath — the most important sentence in the chapter. True prophecy speaks God's word regardless of political consequences.
2. **22:19-22 — the heavenly council**: Micaiah's vision reveals the deliberative process behind the scenes: YHWH, the heavenly host, and a deceiving spirit. This is the most explicit depiction of the divine council in the historical books.
3. **22:34 — "drew the-bow in-his-innocence"**: The archer who kills Ahab acts "innocently" — without aiming. The randomness of the shot is the precision of divine judgment. Ahab's disguise fails because God's word cannot be evaded.
4. **22:38 — dogs lick his blood**: The fulfillment of Elijah's prophecy (21:19). The detail about prostitutes washing adds ritual defilement to the scene — Ahab's death is as degraded as his life.
5. **22:54 — end of 1 Kings**: The book ends with another evil king on Israel's throne — the cycle continues into 2 Kings without resolution.

— EMET
